pages.title: Pop. 23
pages.text: Pop. 23: the ones who stayed, or came back. Nobody has changed the sign since. Most of the houses are dark, their curtains drawn.

pages.title: The Old Stone
pages.text: It hums at night. A crack runs down it, and shards break off along the crack. It wants them back.

blanks.fill: Given enough shards, it wakes, and the surges out there grow gentler while it is awake.

pages.title: Two weeks
pages.text: NAPO told the whole town to leave, a street at a time, with only what it could carry. Back in two weeks, the notice says. It has been a lot longer than two weeks.

pages.title: The verge
pages.text: Where the town waited its turn to leave, what would not fit in the cars still waits: suitcases, boxes, a rocking chair, a piano under a tarp. They were coming back for it.

pages.title: The sawmill
pages.text: Stonebrook was a logging town. The mill shut for a winter and never opened again. Somebody asked which spring, in pencil.

pages.title: The Okadas
pages.text: An older couple, and tidy: everything under a sheet, the boxes they could not take stacked by the door. Their calendar says Home, two weeks on.

pages.title: The Hales
pages.text: Nora was seven. She drew the lights in the woods on the back of a NAPO form: Hale, D. Motor pool. Half the town worked for NAPO.

pages.title: The Dahls
pages.text: A young couple with a baby. Their street was called at nine, and they went that night. The crib would not fit in the car, so it stayed.

pages.title: The Lindqvists
pages.text: Dad filed the saws at the mill. Their list says what to take and what to leave: the piano stayed on the verge, and Mrs. Okada said let the bird go.

pages.title: The Near Woods
pages.text: Out here energy drains, and the deeper in, the faster. The street lights only help to see by. Only a fire gives it back.

pages.title: The Napoland Zone
pages.text: NAPO's name for everything inside its line. Stonebrook called it Napoland first. Keep to the road after dark, its sign says.

pages.title: The lamp with no wires
pages.text: A street light with no wires running to it. It was on when someone found it. It gives light, and no warmth.

pages.title: The listening post
pages.text: NAPO listened to the stones here. They hum back to the Old Stone, the sign says. It carried some of them off in cages, to listen closer.

pages.title: The burned jeep
pages.text: NAPO field survey, unit 7. Burned out to the frame, and the firs beside it with it. The keys are still in it.

pages.title: Surges
pages.text: The woods grow restless, and then a surge rolls in from the deep end toward home, on the same clock every time. Out in the open where it has passed, energy drains three times as fast.

blanks.fill: The drain stops under a street light, and under a roof.

pages.title: Storms
pages.text: The sky darkens, the fog closes in, the lightning blinks. Out in a storm the wind and the lightning wear me down, and it soaks me through.

blanks.fill: A roof keeps all of it off.

pages.title: Flashes
pages.text: A patch of ground starts to glow, faster and brighter, and then it bursts: a spark, or a burn.

blanks.ask: Standing in it when it bursts... ?
blanks.fill: Standing in it when it bursts drains six times as fast. Step off while it glows.

pages.title: Watchers
pages.text: Tall and pale in the trees, with a blank face. Closer every time I look back. They never stand in the light, or by a fire.

blanks.fill: It stops when someone looks at it.

pages.title: Skulkers
pages.text: Something long and low lies in the ferns at night, and in storms. It came after me, a little slower than I run, and then it gave up.

blanks.fill: Before it comes, the ferns rustle.

pages.title: Tall grass
pages.text: Knee-high grass to crouch in. Something hunted close by, and never noticed me. It keeps nothing else off: not the rain, not the cold.

blanks.fill: A chase ends at its edge.

pages.title: Live shards
pages.text: A shard that broke loose while the woods were restless, still humming with it. Everyone can see the light over whoever carries one, and so can the watchers.

blanks.fill: It stays live for a few minutes, then fades into a plain shard. Stashed fresh, it is worth the most.

pages.title: Food from the woods
pages.text: Huckleberries ripen out in the open, fiddleheads uncurl by the water, fir tips are soft and green at the ends of the branches. At any fire that burns they cook into something that keeps me going.

pages.title: Chanterelles
pages.text: Golden mushrooms in the moss under the firs, smelling of apricots. There one hour and gone the next.

blanks.fill: They come up in the rain, and last a while after it stops.

pages.title: The South Road
pages.text: NAPO's old grounds. No surge reaches it, and nothing watches from its trees. Its danger is how far it goes.

pages.title: The Observatory
pages.text: The National Anomalous Phenomena Observatory came to study the hum in the radios and the compasses. Restricted grounds, staff only, its sign still says.

pages.title: The jam
pages.text: Everyone left down this road. Here the line of leavers stopped and never moved again: doors open, a trunk up, the luggage still between the cars.

pages.title: NAPO Bunker
pages.text: Shelter for NAPO's staff during events. Ruth keeps its fire going for whoever comes down the road.

pages.title: The research station
pages.text: All visitors report to the front desk. Nobody sits at the desk now. Vera is still in the laboratory, listening.

pages.title: The Tower
pages.text: Red and white, with a dish turned to the woods and a red light that blinks day and night. Danger: high voltage. Walt strung its wire.

pages.title: The motor pool
pages.text: NAPO's box trucks, parked in a row behind a fence. Vehicles sign out at the front desk. Nobody signed these out.

pages.title: The field site
pages.text: Scorched gravel, instruments, and a mast where NAPO listened closest. Keep out, the sign says.

pages.title: Sample cages
pages.text: Rocks NAPO carried out of the woods, caged in steel mesh and tagged, to listen to. They glow a little, day and night. One tag names no place at all.

pages.title: The quarantine line
pages.text: No one passes, in or out, by order of the Observatory. Under it someone wrote: They said two weeks. Nobody has kept the checkpoint in years.

pages.title: Vera's radio
pages.text: Always on. Under the static a low hum rises and falls. The card taped to it counts the days she has been listening.

pages.title: The checkpoint log
pages.text: The last guard wrote it day by day: the road closed, the last cars through, no relief. Then only the woods lighting up every forty minutes.

pages.title: The trappers' trail
pages.text: The trappers went up it in pairs. Up there the woods are older, and they wear you down twice as fast. Feed the fire going in, the sign says, so it still burns on the way out.

pages.title: The Far Woods
pages.text: Old growth, older than the town: firs and cedars too wide to reach around, ferns to the waist. Out here I tire twice as fast as in the Near Woods. There is one fire, and nobody keeps it: whoever passes feeds it.

pages.title: The trapper
pages.text: His tally in pencil: marten, fisher, and one lynx, underlined twice. Farther in, his traps came back sprung, and empty. Never alone past the gorge, he wrote, and leave wood for the next one.

pages.title: Camp 4
pages.text: Stonebrook Timber Co., Camp 4: the loggers' last camp. The bunkhouse has fallen in, the yarder rusted where it stood, and the cable is still on its spools. Chalked on the board: back in the spring.

pages.title: The hollow
pages.text: NAPO kept a post out here, in a dark hollow where the rocks hum back louder than anywhere. Its crews came two at a time and logged every visit. Its mast is snapped halfway, and its light is dead.

pages.title: Cedar bark
pages.text: Long dry strips off the old cedars. It burns hot and slow, nearly as long as resin, and it weighs less.

pages.title: Old batteries
pages.text: Heavy dry cells stamped NAPO, with a little charge still in them. Its field kit ran on them: the radios, the lamps, the instruments. Nothing I can make takes them yet.

pages.title: Resin tears
pages.text: A drop of old resin gone hard and clear, with a seed caught inside. Only the oldest cedars weep them. Carried deep in, one makes the going a little easier.

pages.title: Gate N-1
pages.text: The farthest thing NAPO built, and it never went through it. A steel gate too heavy for one: it moves only when two pull together. From the far side it opens for anyone, so nobody is shut in.

pages.title: The Burn
pages.text: A forest the answer burned. The firs still stand, black and bare, over ground grey with ash. Out here I tire three times as fast as in the Near Woods. It never rains, and there is one fire.

pages.title: The line book
pages.text: The trapper was up here the night of the answer. Green light over the ridge, then white, and every needle swung the same way and stayed. The fire came down in the night and went round his cabin.

pages.title: The line cabin
pages.text: He stayed a week after, crossing off the days. The rocks stayed warm, the needles stayed turned, and his traps came back empty, and clean. Then the crossing off stops.

pages.title: The black creek
pages.text: The creek runs dark with the ash in its bed. The ferns came back beside it first, and whatever lies in ferns came with them.

pages.title: The windfall
pages.text: Where the burned firs came down across each other, the old trap line is under them. The trapper cut his way round and kept going.

pages.title: The scar
pages.text: A long trench of bare ground run together into glass, where the light came up out of it. The rocks along it ring, warm to the touch. Nobody should come here alone, the plate says, and nobody should sleep here.

pages.title: Fused glass
pages.text: Sand and stone melted green and cooled with bubbles in it. Still warm. Two lumps ring when they touch. Nothing I can make takes it yet, but it is worth the carry.

pages.title: The high line
pages.text: The trappers fixed a rope up the ice, knotted every arm's length. It holds with three on it and not with fewer. Coming down, it holds for anyone.

pages.title: The Ridge
pages.text: Above the Burn the woods climb out of the firs into snow. It is always winter up here, and I tire four times as fast as in the Near Woods. My steps stay in the snow behind me, and so do everyone else's.

pages.title: The high hut
pages.text: The trappers' hut under the ice: three bunks, three names to every trip on the wall. The needles turn up here too, they wrote, but slowly, as if they were thinking.

pages.title: The icefall
pages.text: A slope of old ice straight up from the hut to the snowfield, between walls of rock. Nobody climbs it in boots. In crampons it is the short way up.

pages.title: The switchbacks
pages.text: The long way up zigzags through the last of the firs. When it snows up here I see a few steps and no more, and the tracks in the snow are the way.

pages.title: The tarn
pages.text: Still, dark water in a hollow of the snow. The edges never thaw and the middle never freezes, which is backwards, the trappers noticed.

pages.title: The crest
pages.text: The top of the Ridge, wind-scoured rock, the rime stones along it humming like the rocks that hum back. Up here the needles spin, and at night the snow beyond glows from underneath.

pages.title: Rime quartz
pages.text: Clear quartz off the crest's stones, furred with rime that will not melt by any fire. It hums in the hand. Hard enough to put a point on steel.

pages.title: The Marsh
pages.text: Off the loggers' corduroy road the ground gives way to bog. The town cut its peat out here, before. The mist never lifts, and I tire three times as fast as in the Near Woods. The lights on the water are not lanterns.

pages.title: The cutters' hut
pages.text: The peat cutters slept here in May, a line a day in their book. The last May the lights were on the water again, and they left the peat stacked to dry. Nobody came back for it in August.

pages.title: Channel boards
pages.text: The boards across the channels rot, and whoever passes mends them, a few sheets of scrap at a time. While they stand the way is short. When they fall in, it is the long way round again, for everyone.

pages.title: The channel's head
pages.text: The long way round the first channel, by its head. Slow, but it is always there, whatever the boards are doing.

pages.title: The peat cuttings
pages.text: Long dark banks where the town cut peat, the spades still stuck in them. A brick of it burns all night: a whole shelter fire kept going by one armful.

pages.title: The channel's foot
pages.text: The long way round the second channel, by its foot. Past it the reeds get thick, and at night something lies in them.

pages.title: The black pool
pages.text: Dark water in a ring of reeds, and stones in the reeds that hum back like the ring in the Near Woods. The lights gather over it. Nobody fishes it, and nobody should wait for the lights to come to them.

pages.title: Peat
pages.text: Dark, crumbling, smelling of smoke before it is lit. It burns low and long, far longer than resin. Worth carrying to whichever fire out there nobody keeps.

pages.title: Glowcaps
pages.text: Glowcaps grow in the damp. Crushed, they glow for a day: good for marking a way.

pages.title: Fir resin
pages.text: Amber sap from the old firs, lying in the grass. It burns slow and bright: the best thing to feed a fire.

pages.title: Cloth scraps
pages.text: Curtains and blankets people left, torn into strips. Dry, so it catches fast, and it burns fast. The workbench wants a lot of it.

pages.title: Scrap metal
pages.text: Rust from the wrecks and cabins nobody came back for. Good for patching things. Carry too much and I tire faster.

pages.title: Copper wire
pages.text: From where the old line came down. Now and then it still hums in the hand.

blanks.ask: More of it turns up by the poles... ?
blanks.fill: More of it turns up by the poles on green nights.

pages.title: Anomaly shards
pages.text: Warm even in the cold, with a light of their own. They turn up far out. The Old Stone wants them back.

blanks.ask: By the old poles they turn up... ?
blanks.fill: By the old poles they turn up while a storm blows.

pages.title: Strange objects
pages.text: Something that was not there the day before. Out here it is too dark to tell what it is.

blanks.fill: It shows what it is only in the light, in town.

pages.title: Thermoses
pages.text: Hot coffee, left by a fire for whoever comes next. Somebody keeps leaving them.

pages.title: Road flares
pages.text: Red road flares from the gloveboxes. Lit, one burns for most of a minute, and nothing comes near while it does.

pages.title: NAPO's first aid
pages.text: Hand warmers and rad tablets, still sealed, from NAPO's first-aid stores. One keeps the cold off me for a while, the other the glow. A second one does not add up: it only starts the time again.

pages.title: A meal for the trip
pages.text: A meal cooked at a fire lasts the trip: until I am home again, or I fall. Two at a time, never the same one twice. Eaten at home before I set out, it goes the whole way with me.

pages.title: Charms
pages.text: Some strange things work while they ride in the bag. A warm pebble keeps the rain out, a hollow feather lightens the load, a humming bead keeps things from clinging.

pages.title: Hitchhikers
pages.text: At night, far enough out and away from the light, something climbs onto my back. I tire faster while it rides.

blanks.fill: It lets go at a street light, a fire, a roof or a flare.

pages.title: Aurora nights
pages.text: Every third night the sky goes green, and the watchers are faster under it.

blanks.fill: The dead power lines hum and glow on green nights.

pages.title: The lamp went out
pages.text: The lamp with no wires is dark. It was burning a moment ago, and nothing I did put it out. The poles along the line stand as they always did, each leaning its own way. Whoever did this was standing right here.

pages.title: The Reservoir
pages.text: The brook comes down out of a lake behind a dam, built to drive the mill in town. The surges die before they reach it. What moves up here is the water.

pages.title: The dam
pages.text: The Timber Co. held the brook here to run the mill, and the water drowned the valley of the first farms. NAPO's maps show only lake.

pages.title: Low water
pages.text: The lake drew back and left the old valley lying in the air: fences, stumps, a lane, a car. The mud holds my weight. It doesn't stay out for long.

blanks.fill: The water comes back fast, and carries whoever is still out on the bed to the shore, soaked.

pages.title: Caught by the water
pages.text: The water came home while I was still out on the bed. It took my feet and set me down on the shore, soaked through and shaking. The lake doesn't wait for anyone.

pages.title: The Sister
pages.text: A standing stone in the middle of the old valley, the Old Stone's shape, and whole. The old folks called her the Sister. She was under water sixty years, and nobody heard her hum.

pages.title: The drowned farm
pages.text: Fences in the mud, a house fallen in, a kitchen table where it stood. The first farms were here before the dam. They had to leave too, long before NAPO told anyone to.

pages.title: NAPO's letter
pages.text: The week before the answer NAPO asked the keeper to draw the reservoir down three metres, for a survey of the valley floor. She wrote no across it. Someone else wrote that they pay.

pages.title: The sluice book
pages.text: Jon Brandt ran the boat and the sluice: forty years of openings, one turn or two. The last is the week before the answer, at two in the morning. Nine turns, and no name after it.

pages.title: The Turning
pages.text: A clearing in old firs, a stump in the middle, and one notch cut in a fir: the ranger's mark. A trail leaves it on every side, and the trees all look alike. The ranger's board by the ring said this wood turns you round.

pages.title: Two notches
pages.text: The same clearing again, fir for fir and fern for fern, but a cairn in the middle where the stump was, and two notches in the fir. One stone at its edge hums like the ring's.

pages.title: Three notches
pages.text: The same clearing a third time, three notches in the fir, and NAPO's survey stakes running across it and on out of it. NAPO came this far, and kept going.

pages.title: The ranger's camp
pages.text: Her camp: a hut like the one by the lamp, the fire in, the kettle warm, the bunk made, and nobody about. She drew the Turning on the wall, the same clearing three times.

pages.title: The ranger's board
pages.text: A board by the ring of stones, in the ranger's hand: the wood past it turns you round. Whoever goes in comes out by the stones again, facing them, as if they never left.

pages.title: Line T
pages.text: NAPO surveyed even this: a line of stakes and a tag that says the survey goes on. It never says where it ended. Their stakes are the only straight thing in the Turning.

pages.title: On. Mornings.
pages.text: An arrow cut in a fir at the back of her camp, pointing on, and two words in her hand under it. Mornings: as if the way on were only there some of the time, or as if she only dared it by day.

pages.title: Her calendar
pages.text: She crossed off every day since the answer, past the end of the calendar and onto the wall, row under row. The last row is fresh. Whoever keeps the count keeps it still.

pages.title: Said back
pages.text: The woods' own sign, letter for letter, backwards. Every path I knew is here the wrong way round, and the sky is green and does not move.

pages.title: Both ways wrong
pages.text: The crossroads sign, backwards, points to the pond one way and the old cabin the other. Here both are on the wrong side. It was right once, before it was said back.

pages.title: The lamp, lit
pages.text: The lamp nobody wired burns here, as it burned in the Near Woods the night of the answer. The sign under it says so, backwards.

pages.title: NAPO, backwards
pages.text: Even NAPO's sign is said back. Whatever heard that night heard NAPO's paint too, and every word on it.

pages.title: The post, said back
pages.text: NAPO's mast by the ring, and its sign asking nobody to move the stones, backwards. The ring hums here as loud as anywhere I have stood.

pages.title: The whole jeep
pages.text: NAPO's survey jeep, the one that burned out off the road: here it is whole, not a mark of fire on it, and the bonnet is warm. Here it never burned.

pages.title: No trail
pages.text: The sign for the trappers' trail, backwards, at the foot of nothing: past it the firs close in. The woods only said back what they heard.

pages.title: Her board, backwards
pages.text: The ranger's board by the ring, said back, the paint as fresh as hers. She put it up long after that night. Then how is it here?

pages.title: The fallen lookout
pages.text: The Timber Co.'s lookout, said back and fallen in on itself, its sign still standing, backwards. The one in the Near Woods stands. This one came down, or was never quite heard.

pages.title: No town
pages.text: The road runs on to where town should be, and the firs close over it. A sign says Stonebrook backwards, and Pop. 23. Past it, nothing was said back.
